theorem: For every equivariant conditional noise kernel K, fixing a condition rho reduces symmetry from G to its stabilizer G_rho. The conditional output law is G_rho-invariant, so it can distinguish only G_rho-orbits. Uniform conditioning retains all D12 symmetry; delta_0 and an even localized heat state reduce to the reflection stabilizer and can select vertex 0 but not an orientation; a chiral condition has trivial stabilizer and supplies both localization and orientation. Hence state-conditioned noise does not create a selector ex nihilo: the orbit information absent from G_rho is carried by the conditioning state.
